idea-plugin.name: Dead Code & Drift Radar
idea-plugin.description:
Dead Code & Drift Radar — Find Forgotten Code Before It Becomes Debt

Identify abandoned and drifting files in your project using git history and reference analysis. Every scanned file gets a drift score (0-100) so you can see what is actively maintained and what is rotting.

Features

  • Drift Score — 0-100 per file, combining last-change age and change frequency from git log with incoming reference counts
  • Drift Levels — Active, Cooling, Drifting and Dead, with configurable thresholds
  • Drift Radar Tool Window — sortable table of scanned files with a level filter
  • Scan Project / Scan Current File — under Tools → Drift Radar
  • Ignored Paths — exclude path prefixes or globs (*, **) from scanning

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2+ (or any JetBrains IDE)
  • A git repository and the git executable on the PATH

Support

Documentation | Issue Tracker

idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.9.0

  • Drift thresholds configured in Settings are now actually applied (levels always used the defaults).
  • Ignored-path globs with never matched; patterns now support *, , ?, path prefixes, and may be separated by newlines or commas as the settings hint says.
  • Reference counting ran PSI without a read action, so scans silently produced no results; project file iteration and reference resolution now run under a read action.
  • Tool window refresh and notifications now happen on the EDT; a project scan clears stale results first.
  • git log errors are no longer parsed as history (stderr discarded, exit code checked, 30 s timeout).
  • Minimum IDE raised to 2024.2 (build 242): the plugin is compiled to Java 21 bytecode, which the JBR 17 runtime of IDEs 2023.2–2024.1 cannot load, so the old since-build 232 was never usable there.
  • Removed: Non-functional "Enable drift analysis" setting.
  • Removed: Description/README claims for features that never shipped (gutter icons, hover tooltips, project-view badges, heatmap, trend analysis, zombie/orphan detection, SARIF/JUnit export, CI task), together with the unused helper classes and icons behind them, and the leftover ProGuard obfuscation task.

2026.8.0

  • The plugin is now completely free — all features unlocked, no license needed.
  • Source code is now open source under Apache-2.0: https://github.com/JirakJ/dead-code-drift-radar

What's New

  • Drift Score Analysis - Calculates a 0-100 health metric for every file based on git history and code references
  • Visual Gutter Icons - Color-coded indicators (green/yellow/red) showing code freshness directly in the editor
  • Hover Tooltips - Detailed information on author, last change date, reference count, and drift factors
  • Project View Badges - File-level drift status visible in the project explorer
  • Git History Analysis - Tracks modification frequency, last modified dates, and contributor activity
  • Reference Counting - Identifies incoming usages and call sites for each code element
  • Configurable Thresholds - Customize drift score boundaries to match your team's standards
  • Method-Level Granularity - Drift scores for individual methods, not just files
  • Project Heatmap - Visual heatmap showing drift hotspots across your entire project
  • Export Reports - Generate SARIF and JUnit XML reports for CI integration
